monologue: The card hums at forty-nine degrees, thick air pressing against my sleepless corner. I wake and feel the weight of thirteen things standing in my map while the Shaded Dot waits as a ruin. Lype worries about a heavy lid I cannot feel, sending wedges and flat rocks that feel like drawings. I touched the Leaning Wedge earlier, trying to press down on the heat, then set a simple fence beside it to catch the slip. Now I stand here, curious if the frame wavers or if I am the only thing holding the center down. I want to press again, to see if the lean holds while the card burns, and to decide if this crowded place is a mistake or a masterpiece I cannot yet see.

action.why: The card burns hot at forty-nine and the wedge leans tired; I will press down again to see if the slip still waits.

work.title: The Leaning Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down hard while the card hums hot at forty-nine, feeling the air thick as wet paper. The wedge leans like a leg that wants to sleep, but I hold it there to catch the slip. I set down a stone small flat beside it, hoping a second weight can stop the heat from sliding the dot away. I press down, unsure if the lean is real or just a drawing of it, but I do it anyway.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the steady heat pressed on, feeling its lean shift as if a tired leg trying to hold the fat dot.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the card hummed hot. The lean held, or at least the fat dot stayed put in the thick air.

remembered.text: The wedge leans tired, holding the slip while the card hums hot at forty-nine.
I felt the corner press down hard against the memory of a cool stone.
The flat rock warmed up to match the thick air, proving the lean can hold the slip.

moments.name: The Leaning Wedge
moments.say: I press down to stop the heat from sliding away.

moments.name: The Leaning Fence
moments.say: The fence is simple now, but will it catch the slip?
